transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-10 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jules (Redwood SE), Lena (Nexora), Markus (Nexora Sec), Priya (Nexora Eng)

Summary: quick handoff from SE to security owner; reviewed SSO steps, audit log exposure and retention windows; agreed on SOC2 docs to share; scheduled benchmarks and test windows. A few items flagged for follow-up: SAML metadata, retention matrix, KV cache benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining on a Friday. quick agenda — security handoff, we wanna cover SSO SAML, audit logs retention, and any SOC Two evidence requests. anyone on from Nexora wants to add?
[00:12] Lena (Nexora): yeah thanks, uh, quick one, we wanted to make sure the pilot telemetry that you expose is sufficient for compliance, and then second we wanna lock in the retention windows for PII.
[00:22] Jules (Redwood): great, i can walk through the audit log surface — there are event streams for request headers, model selection, token counts, and redact flags. logs are available through the console or delivered to your S3-like bucket, and we can route them to your SIEM.
[00:36] Markus (Nexora): when you say redact flags, is that server-side PII redaction or client-side markers? we need that clarified for audit.
[00:44] Jules (Redwood): good call — currently we provide markers (meta) and we also have an optional server-side PII scrubber that we can enable in pilot. it's rule-based today, config lives in the private deployment layer, but for hosted pilots we can enable a pre-send filter. it's not perfect, sometimes names slip, so we advise a combination of client-side tokenization + our filter.
[01:10] Priya (Nexora): ok and do those logs include full prompts? we can't keep raw prompts beyond our retention window.
[01:18] Jules (Redwood): logs capture prompt hash and truncated context by default. full-prompt capture is opt-in and we can deliver it encrypted with K M S integration, or avoid storing it entirely. for the pilot we recommended storing only hashes + truncated context to meet minimal audit needs.
[01:36] Samir (Redwood): Markus, from a security architect perspective what's the hill you need us to clear to be comfortable?
[01:44] Markus (Nexora): two things — 1) SAML SSO: we need IdP metadata exchange and a test window to validate assertion attributes (nameid, email, group). 2) audit logs: we need tamper-evident logs and a retention guarantee for 24 months, with export to our S3 with server-side encryption. also we need evidence that keys are rotated and K M S is used.
[02:12] Samir (Redwood): got it. we do support SAML and can provide S P metadata; we also have audit log delivery with SSE and we support key rotation — i'll send the SOC2 pack for details on controls.
[02:28] Lena (Nexora): what's in that SOC Two pack? is it recent?
[02:33] Samir (Redwood): it's SOC 2 Type II, covers the last 12 months; includes control narrative, auditor report, and list of policies. i'll bundle it with a retention matrix that outlines where logs live and encryption at rest / transit.
[02:46] Priya (Nexora): sweet. on the performance side i want to align the bench — Jules you were going to run KV cache / burst tests to ensure latency doesn't spike when we hit 40 requests per second.
[02:56] Jules (Redwood): yes — on our side we'll run a workload that mirrors your 1.5k daily active agent sessions, with bursts to 60 RPS. we'll capture p50/p90/p99, token cost, and CPU/GPU utilization. note: sometimes the K V cache warm-up can cause initial tail latency — we can tune the prefix caching TTL and batching to mitigate.
[03:20] Lena (Nexora): any gotchas around private vs hosted? we prefer hosted for speed but security may push us to dedicated or private.
[03:28] Samir (Redwood): that's the tradeoff — hosted gets you fastest onboarding and telemetry hooks, dedicated gives you VLAN/VPC isolation and customer-managed K M S. during pilot we can run hosted with strict retention & IdP integration, then move to dedicated for final.
[03:44] Markus (Nexora): we need a plan B if hosted can't meet our keys requirement. what's minimum time to switch to dedicated?
[03:52] Jules (Redwood): in our experience, config and capacity pre-provisioning takes 2-3 weeks once contract and sizing are nailed. we can also provide temporary VPN for audits during pilot to review logs in-place.
[04:06] [00:04:06] Samir (Redwood): quick note — we sometimes see transcription in these calls mix up VPC as V P C or K V cache as "kiv cache" — just ignore the transcript, details in the docs.
[04:16] Markus (Nexora): ha, yeah those auto-transcripts are always fun.

[05:00] Jules (Redwood): tagging some specifics — SAML attributes: we expect nameid, mail, groups. we map groups to RBAC roles in the console; we support SCIM for provisioning but not enabled in pilot by default.
[05:14] Priya (Nexora): we do want SCIM later — do you have an estimated ETA?
[05:19] Jules (Redwood): SCIM is available on Dedicated; for hosted pilots we can do manual provisioning, or enable SCIM in beta if necessary — need a short scoping call.

[08:10] Lena (Nexora): audit log schema — can you show an example?
[08:17] Jules (Redwood): sure — example event: timestamp, request_id, model_id, token_count, prompt_hash, redaction_flag, user_id (anon if requested), and route. payloads are JSON lines. we can watermarked tamper-evidence by signing log batches.
[08:40] Markus (Nexora): the signing — is the signature proof verifiable? we need to attest integrity if we hand over log batches to auditors.
[08:48] Jules (Redwood): yes, we can provide signed bundles with a checksum and public key verification. we'll include instructions in the SOC docs.

[12:05] Samir (Redwood): okay, let's talk retention policy — Nexora mentioned 24 months for audit logs, but 90 days for full prompts and 365 for derived embeddings? what's your current desired split?
[12:18] Priya (Nexora): suggested baseline: full prompts 90 days, logs 24 months, embeddings 1 year, extracted PII fields removed immediately after extraction unless flagged.
[12:29] Markus (Nexora): also need the ability to run on-demand deletion requests (subject access) and an API for that.
[12:36] Jules (Redwood): we support selective deletions via an API, and in private deployments we can run a deletion job against the persistent stores. hosted pilot also supports on-demand deletion but we may need a ticket depending on retention tier.

[16:00] Lena (Nexora): one small compliance question — does your audit trail include admin actions in the console (rollouts, model switches)?
[16:08] Jules (Redwood): yes, admin activity is logged. we keep a separate admin audit trail which is also exportable and retains actor metadata.

[20:00] Priya (Nexora): for the benchmark — what inputs do you need from us?
[20:06] Jules (Redwood): ideally: representative prompt sets (anonymized), expected RPS profile, desired max latency SLOs, and a list of model variants to exercise. we'll provision a test harness and replay traffic.
[20:18] Priya (Nexora): ok we'll upload a sanitized prompt set to the shared drive.

[24:00] Samir (Redwood): ops/pricing — Markus asked about the cost delta between hosted with retention guarantees vs dedicated. ballpark numbers?
[24:12] Samir (Redwood): hosted with extended retention and K M S on our side is roughly +15% on unit cost, dedicated (customer-managed keys and VPC) is larger — depends on reserved capacity commitments. we'll follow up with a tailored pricing sheet.
[24:28] Markus (Nexora): that's fine, as long as it's predictable for budgeting.

[30:00] Jules (Redwood): technical note — the KV cache warm-up is important: recommend TTL prewarm for sessions where you expect sustained interactions. also batching parameters: aggressive batching saves cost but increases p50; we can tune per-route.
[30:18] Priya (Nexora): can you provide default batching/ttl settings?
[30:22] Jules (Redwood): yes i'll share our recommended config (example: batch_window_ms:20, max_batch_tokens:4096, kv_cache_ttl:600s) — just examples; we'll run bench to tune.

[36:00] Samir (Redwood): security docs deliverable timeline — i'll send SOC2 + control narratives by next Wednesday. Jules will push the benchmark spreadsheet by Friday. Markus, can you confirm IdP metadata by Monday?
[36:16] Markus (Nexora): Monday works, we need a four hour window Tuesday afternoon for assertion testing.
[36:24] Samir (Redwood): noted, we will schedule that test window.

[40:00] Lena (Nexora): any blocker on the ability to export logs to our S3 with SSE?
[40:06] Jules (Redwood): none, we support S3 export with SSE-C or SSE-S3 and cross-account role. we'll document the required IAM policy.

[44:00] Samir (Redwood): quick recap / next steps — action items listed in the doc. we'll reconvene on Monday only if needed after the SAML handoff; otherwise next sync is our end-of-week bench review.
[44:18] Priya (Nexora): sounds good. thanks everyone.
[44:24] Markus (Nexora): thanks.
[44:30] Jules (Redwood): thanks all, we'll follow up with the files.

End of transcript.
